chapters.name: Demand and Supply
chapters.introduction: Demand and supply are the fundamental forces of any market economy. This chapter covers law of demand, supply, elasticity, and market equilibrium.
chapters.whyItMatters: 15-20 marks. Demand-supply diagrams and equilibrium questions always appear.

topics.name: Law of Demand
topics.explanation: Law of Demand: Other things being equal, as price increases, quantity demanded decreases (inverse relationship). Demand curve slopes downward to the right. Exceptions: Giffen goods, conspicuous goods, necessities during emergency.
topics.examTip: Always draw the demand curve in answers — it earns diagram marks.

topics.name: Law of Supply and Market Equilibrium
topics.explanation: Law of Supply: As price increases, quantity supplied increases (direct relationship). Supply curve slopes upward. Equilibrium: Price where Qd = Qs. Surplus: Qs > Qd → price falls. Shortage: Qd > Qs → price rises.
keyPoints: Equilibrium: Demand curve intersects Supply curve
topics.examTip: Show equilibrium as the crossing point of demand and supply curves.
topics.formula: Elasticity of Demand = % change in Qd / % change in Price

chapters.name: Market System
chapters.introduction: Types of market structures: perfect competition, monopoly, monopolistic competition, and oligopoly.
chapters.whyItMatters: 10-12 marks. Market types and their characteristics are definitional questions.

topics.name: Types of Market
topics.explanation: Perfect Competition: Many buyers/sellers, homogeneous products, no barriers. Monopoly: Single seller, unique product, high barriers. Oligopoly: Few large sellers (e.g., telecom). Monopolistic: Many sellers, differentiated products (e.g., restaurants).
keyPoints: Nepal examples: Nepal Telecom vs private ISPs
topics.examTip: Give local Nepali examples when discussing market structures.

chapters.name: National Income and Inflation
chapters.introduction: GDP, GNP, NNP, per capita income, and circular flow of income. Inflation types, causes, and effects on the economy.
chapters.whyItMatters: 15-18 marks. Definitions and differences between GDP/GNP/NNP are standard.

topics.name: GDP, GNP and NNP
topics.explanation: GDP = Total market value of all goods and services produced within a country in a year (regardless of nationality). GNP = GDP + Net factor income from abroad. NNP = GNP − Depreciation. Per Capita Income = National Income / Total Population.
topics.examTip: Know all formulas and be able to calculate with given values.
topics.formula:
GNP = GDP + Net Factor Income from Abroad (NFIA)
NNP = GNP − Depreciation
Per Capita Income = NNP / Population

topics.name: Inflation
topics.explanation: Inflation: general, sustained rise in price level. Types: demand-pull (excess demand) and cost-push (rising production costs). Effects: reduces purchasing power, affects savings, widens inequality. Controlled by monetary policy (NRB raising interest rates) and fiscal policy.
keyPoints: Cost-push: oil price rise, wage rise
NRB controls money supply to fight inflation
topics.examTip: Use Nepal examples: NRB raising CRR and SLR to control inflation.

chapters.name: Economic Development of Nepal
chapters.introduction: Nepal's development challenges: poverty, unemployment, low productivity, dependence on agriculture, and foreign aid.
chapters.whyItMatters: 15-18 marks. Nepal's economic development is always tested with current data.

topics.name: Poverty and Employment
topics.explanation: Poverty: income below minimum threshold. Absolute poverty: cannot meet basic needs. Relative poverty: below national average. Unemployment types: frictional, structural, cyclical. Nepal's poverty rate ~17%. Major employer: agriculture, followed by services sector.
topics.examTip: Use recent data and government statistics (NPC, CBS) in answers for full marks.
